Seminar Title:

Water Quality Assessment and Application of Chemically Activated Corn Cob Biochar as an Adsorbent for Removal of Ca2+ and Mg2+ Ions from Ground Hard Water Samples from an Industrial Zone

Seminar Type:

Progress Seminar

Department:

Chemistry

Speaker Name:

Sangram Keshari Dash ( Rollno : 919cy5103)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Seminar Hall, Chemistry Department

Date and Time:

11 Nov 2026 04.30 PM

Contact:

Braja Gopal Mishra

Abstract:

Water pollution from multiple sources in industrial regions poses a severe ecological crisis. This study evaluates the water quality of Ghatsila, Jharkhand, India&mdasha prominent industrial hub from 2020 to 2025 across pre-monsoon, monsoon, and post-monsoon seasons, while simultaneously developing a sustainable remediation strategy. Physicochemical and heavy metal analyses revealed Water Quality Index (WQI) variations between 57.6 and 158.0. The assessment proved that hardness, TDS, Fe, Cu, and Ni are primary pollutants requiring targeted treatment.&nbspTo address severe water hardness, a low-cost, eco-friendly adsorbent was fabricated via alkali activation of corn cob biochar pyrolyzed at 300 &degC (MCCB 300). Surface &ndashCOOH and -OH functional groups provided a nucleophilic surface with a strong affinity for positively charged Ca&sup2⁺ and Mg&sup2⁺ ions. Optimization of adsorption parameters through batch experiments revealed an optimal hardness removal efficiency of 92.7% at a 10 g/L dosage and 60-minute contact time for water with an initial hardness of 606 mg/L. Equilibrium isotherm and kinetic models confirmed the adsorption mechanisms. Ultimately, this integrated study successfully pairs advanced statistical water quality assessment with a viable, bio-resource-based solution to soften polluted water in industrial zones
